codeReview.summary: Review failed. The change only adds tests, and the new VAL-CROSS-009/010 coverage does not actually observe the host behaviors it claims to prove. Regressions in refresh-driven timer pacing, idle suppression, active-input pumping, and observed-object coalescing/dependency filtering would still pass this suite.

issues.description: The new VAL-CROSS-009 tests never verify refresh-rate updates or timer enable/disable behavior. `testRefreshRateUpdatesControlRuntimeMinimumFrameInterval`, `testIdleTimerSuppressionWhenNotDirty`, and `testActiveInputDrivesTimerPumping` only check `fakeWindow.useHighResolutionTimer`, which `syncAnimationDriver` sets unconditionally, and `testTimerCadenceCalculationFromRefreshRate` only validates a local helper without exercising `WinSwiftUIWindowHost.syncAnimationDriver(for:)` or any changed `monitorRefreshRate`. A regression where the host stopped propagating refresh-rate changes or stopped suppressing/re-enabling the timer would still pass these tests.

The new VAL-CROSS-010 tests are effectively placeholders. They do not register any observed dependency set, do not wait for the deferred reload task to fire, and do not assert reload/presentation counts or any host state. Three of the tests end in `XCTAssertTrue(true, ...)` after calling `ObservableObjectCenter.shared.notify(...)`, so regressions in same-turn coalescing or dependency filtering would remain invisible.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The host-testing skill asks for explicit observable evidence when presenter selection, refresh pacing, or observed-object batching changes, but there is no documented standard seam for asserting `Win32Window` timer state. The worker attempted to add a `TestableWindowWrapper` after discovering `Win32Window` is final, left that wrapper unused, and fell back to placeholder assertions instead.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Tests/SwiftWindowsCoreLogicTests/WinSwiftUIWindowHostTests.swift:128-150 defines `TestableWindowWrapper`, but the added VAL-CROSS-009/010 tests at lines 705-1071 use plain `Win32Window` instances and placeholder assertions. The transcript skeleton for worker session `afa65e50-5055-444b-8d05-1258bca80d94` explicitly notes the failed subclass attempt and the fallback to a wrapper approach.

summary: Fail: the feature's new host tests do not make VAL-CROSS-009/010 validator-visible because they never assert the timer state or observed-object reload outcomes they describe.
